No.5141/2025, an application of suspension of jail sentence of the appellant and argue the matter finally.
Prayer is allowed.
Accordingly, IA No.5141/2025 is dismissed as withdrawn.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 09.09.2016, at about 1.30 PM, Dr. R. P. Parmar informed police station Agar that on 09.09.2016, the prosecutrix, minor aged about 15 years and daughter of Ramavtar was admitted in the hospital where she delivered a child.

Upon such information, the police went to the hospital and recorded dehati nalisi (Exhibit-P/1) narrated by prosecutrix stating that she resides at Dashera Maidan, Agar and her parents are fruit trolly vendor at the bus stand and she is doing household works.

As per prosecution case, on 01.01.2016 at about 1.00 PM,
appellant/accused entered into the house of the prosecutrix situated near Dashera Maidan and forcefully committed rape upon her without her consent and also threatened her.

Based upon dehati nalisi, FIR (Exhibit-P/12) bearing No.412/2016 was registered on 09.09.2016 against the appellant u/S 376(2)(e), 376(2)(f), 342,
352, 450 and 506 of IPC alongwith Section 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: Due to the aforesaid, the prosecutrix got pregnant.

During investigation, statement of prosecutrix u/S 164 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17027 3 CRA-1905-2018 of Cr.P.C. was recorded and prepared spot map.
Mark-sheet and scholar register of the prosecutrix respectively were recovered for the proof of the prosecutrix's age and the prosecutrix was sent for medical examination.

4. Appellant was arrested and after due investigation, the charge-sheet was filed before the JMFC, Agar, who in turn, committed the case to the Court of Sessions from where the case was transferred to the Trial Court for trial.
Appellant abjured his guilt and prayed for trial.
5. Learned Trial Court after appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence available on record, convicted and sentenced the appellant as mentioned in para-2 of this judgement.

Being aggrieved with the said judgement of conviction and order of sentence, appellant has preferred this appeal for setting aside the impugned judgement and discharging him from the charges alleged against him.

6 The prosecution has examined total 09 witnesses namely, prosecutrix (PW-1),
Ramavtar (PW-2), Kantabai (PW-3), Sunita (PW-4), Mahesh (PW-5), Parmanand Sharma (PW-6), Jagdish Bhatt (PW-7), Jyoti Bhargav (PW-8) and Dr. Pankaj Baghel & Dr. Arti Parmar (PW-9).
After completion of prosecution witnesses, the appellant was examined under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
Appellant took defence that he did not commit any offence and he was falsely implicated in the offence.
He did not examine any witness in his defence.

7. Appellant has preferred this criminal appeal on several grounds but during the course of arguments, learned counsel for the appellant did not press this appeal on Ravi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23282368/
2 merits and has not assailed the finding part of judgement.

sentences.text: She confines her arguments on the point of sentence only and submits that appellant is in jail since 20.09.2016 and prays that since the appellant has already undergone 08 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17027 4 CRA-1905-2018 years and 10 months jail incarceration out of total sentence of 15 years, which is more than 50%, his sentence be reduced to the period already undergone.

Learned counsel for the appellant also submits that the Trial Court erred in ignoring the testimony of the prosecutrix (PW-1), her sister Sunita (PW-4) and her brother-in- law (PW-5) wherein they have stated that age of the prosecutrix is 20 years.

Ramavtar (PW-2) and Kantabai (PW-3), father and mother of the prosecutrix respectively stated that at the time of admission of prosecutrix in the school, her date of birth was written on the basis of assumption.
Hence, this appeal be partly allowed and the sentence awarded to the appellant be reduced to the period already undergone by him.

8. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand while supporting the impugned judgement of conviction and order of sentence submits that the judgement was passed by the Trial Court after proper appreciation of evidence available on record.

He submits that prosecutrix was a minor girl,
aged about 15 years and her statements find support from the medical evidence.
There is nothing material on the record, on the basis of which her statements can be disbelieved or doubted.
The prosecution has very well proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and the same is well reasoned establishing the guilt of the appellant.
Therefore, confirming the impugned judgement of conviction and order of sentence, the appeal filed by the appellant may be dismissed.
9. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

10. Prosecutrix (PW-1) deposed that the appellant was her cousin and lives at neighbourhood and on the date of the incident, when she was alone at her house, appellant entered into the house and forcefully committed rape upon her.
She deposed that the appellant, thereafter, threatened her not to disclose the incident NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17027 5 CRA-1905-2018 otherwise, he will kill her.
She further deposed that she informed about the incident to her mother only after nine months when there was pain in her stomach and the fact came in light that prosecutrix was pregnant.
Prosecutrix's mother (PW-2) deposed that when the prosecutrix complained about pain in stomach, she was taken to hospital where the doctor informed that she is pregnant.

Jyoti Bhargav (PW-8), SHO Police Station, Agar deposed that during investigation of the case, she obtained the school leaving certificate (Exhibit-P/6) of the prosecutrix from Saraswati Shishu Mandir, Agar about the age of the prosecutrix, wherein her date of birth was mentioned as 01.01.2002 and according to which, she was about 15 years of age at the time of incident.
From the statements of aforesaid witnesses as well as medical evidence, there remains no doubt that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was subjected to forceful sexual intercourse.
11. On due consideration of the aforesaid, it is evident that the Trial Court has not committed any error in appreciation of evidence available on record.

Further, it is found that the Court below considered the evidence available on record and correctly found that the case of the prosecution is Ravi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23282368/
3 well supported by the witnesses and documentary testimony.

sentences.text: The procedure was well followed by the prosecution and the witnesses of prosecution have profoundly supported the prosecution case.

The Court below has well considered the material available on record, hence no infirmity is found in the impugned order of conviction passed by the Court below and therefore, the Trial Court was justified in discarding the defence version and convicting the appellant/accused u/S 376(2)(e),
376(2)(f), 342, 352, 450 and 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of the POCSO, Act, 2012, hence the said conviction is liable to be affirmed.

12. So far as the sentence is concerned, the matter is related to the incident NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17027 6 CRA-1905-2018 happened on 01.01.2016, more than nine years ago and the appellant has suffered the ordeal of criminal case since 2016.

On the date of offence i.e.
01.01.2016

, the punishment as prescribed under Section 376(2)(e) and 376(2)(f) of IPC was RI for a term which shall not be less than 10 years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for reminder of that person's natural life and shall also be liable to fine.

Similarly, the punishment u/S 3/4 of the POCSO Act, 2012 was imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than 07 years but which shall extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine.

It is expostulated on behalf of the appellant/accused that it was not a fit case to award sentence of imprisonment more than 07 years and Trial Court has not recorded any reason for inflicting sentence of imprisonment of 12 years u/S 3/4 of the POCSO Act.
Considering the act of the appellant and the rigour of the provisions of POCSO Act, there is no need to let of the accused only for the punishment which he has already suffered as undergone period.

As such the minimum sentence of 07 years prescribed u/S 3/4 of the POCSO Act and minimum sentence of 10 years prescribed u/S 376(2)
(e) and 376(2)(f) of IPC at the relevant date of offence are required to be imposed upon the appellant for his aforesaid Act.
Accordingly, this Court finds it expedient to partly allow this appeal to meet the ends of justice by reducing the sentence with no change in punishment of fine amount.

13. Keeping in view the criminal jurisprudence which encompasses reformative and corrective theory as also the doctrine of proportionality, the sentence of 10 years RI with fine of Rs.500/- u/S 376(2)(e) of IPC, 10 years RI with fine of Rs.500/- u/S 376(2)(f) of IPC and sentence of 07 years RI with fine of Rs.500/- u/S 3/4 of the POCSO Act would serve the purpose.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17027 7 CRA-1905-2018 14.
Accordingly, this appeal is partly allowed to the extent that the sentence u/S 376(2)(e) and 376(2)(f) of the IPC is reduced from 15 years RI to 10 years RI with fine of Rs.500/- under each section.
Similarly, sentence u/S 3/4 of the POCSO Act is reduced from 12 years RI to 07 years RI with fine Rs.500/-.
In case of default of payment of fine, the appellant shall undergo further three months RI on each count.
The total fine amount shall be paid to the victim (PW- 1).
No interference in the sentence u/S 342, 352, 450 and 506 of IPC is warranted.
All the sentences to run concurrently.
